text:
on getting good sleep; I'm convinced the only thing that matters is putting 4-5 miles on the wheels each day

all the other stuff ppl do, the "sleep hygiene" routines, pale in comparison

0 miles = bad sleep, always
5+ miles = best odds (nothing is guaranteed)

five thoughts:

1. "sleep is more important than diet and exercise combined" - think this is factual/not even up for debate

key is u have to be maniacal about it throughout the day, at least while getting new habits in place

from the moment u wake up "what can I do to make sure I sleep good tonight"

once u get used to getting 8 hrs...and then u get 4, and u see how fucked up u are...u recognize that u are literally impaired. it happens, u just adjust for it - "not a good day for me to operate heavy machinery"

2. on walking 5+ miles...it sounds like a lot but once u aggressively break ur day down and look for any chunk of free time - its doable

it takes 2-3 months to put a new habit in place...they say 66 days or something comically accurate, but I agree, 60-90 days of daily discipline/dedicated focus and u can change ur lifestyle

best way to get there is in 2 blocks
-wake up early, train, move around
-early afternoon + sunshine
-if u can do more then do it...more movement >> better sleep. that 7-9 AM block where the sun is out is the holy grail bc ur body clock adjusts, but life/work tend to get in the way. someday...

3. jamming it into ur day

-take every possible phone call "on the hop"...say "let me call u back in 2 min," put on sneakers, go outside.
-stuff like replying to emails which u can do from ur phone, save for later in the day, then do it while walking around
-every possible "meeting," make it "lets just walk around," instead of lunch/drinks/coffee
-take the stairs everywhere
-if u have to be somewhere at 2 PM, and are free at noon, dont sit around doing nothing til 130 and take an uber...start walking there at noon even if its 20 miles away, knock out 5, then get a car when the timing lines up

4. perception

no one will think u are weird for this kind of shit

or, put another way, the ppl who will think u are weird...are the ppl who its okay to be thought weird by.

obsessive/psycho/high-performing mf's are all on this type of time

read bios of many great thinkers or authors and u see most of them walked insane amounts each day (8-10+ miles)

a lot of ppl who are "in shape," end up that way as an accidental output...they move around a lot to settle their mind and to get good sleep.

training is "for sanity, not vanity." everything is performance-driven, results-driven, output-driven...all these little steps and habits are incremental, they compound.

u have to be freakish and maniacal about this stuff, "put yourself first," dont worry abt perception...esp bc most people's response will be "damn thats actually a good idea."

5. on all the other stuff ppl do

theres nothing wrong w all the sleep masks, noise machines etc, but beyond that, the more natural the better

"there is no consequence-free drug"
"what goes up must come down"

everything u put in ur body that isnt natural will either leave u groggy, or refresh u at 90% and not 100%...all the supplements are nonsense, and all booze/drugs/pills come at a cost, esp caffeine which has a 5-6 hr half-life (ie stop drinking it 10-12 hrs before bed)

END>>

ultimately sleep is frustrating, its a unicorn...sometimes it just doesn’t come. all u can do is put urself in position to succeed.

but thats why I wrote this up...ppl do everything, except the most important thing...MOVE AROUND.

"Our nature consists in motion; complete rest is death." - Pascal
